note: Files: iterate-runs:abaybektursun-1115-{000503-1e5f,000525-ea4e,014823-ef56,014833-1daa}/answers.jsonl (Think-SFT hard328) and -1115-{000512-ee03,014843-85d9,000607-0e92,000621-1d7e}/answers.jsonl (Think-SFT MATH-500), fetched to runs/theory-tests/<job>/answers.jsonl. offline.json defers 'first-row rule, finished, wrong, candidate C, cleaning and layout row' to 'the first recipe of this file', which offline.json does not include. I took only the recipe text of the first prediction from studies/theory/results/engine/round-08/theories/r8-m09.json; I did not open its predicted values or any earlier test scripts or results. Implemented: first row per problem_index per file in file order; finished = cap_hit is not True and finish_reason != 'length'; wrong = score_v3 != 1; C = first non-empty line after the last case-sensitive 'Answer:', else the last non-empty line, else ''; cleaning in the stated order: strip, delete '$' and '*', remove one leading '\\[' or '\\(' and one trailing '\\]' or '\\)', remove one trailing '.', then replace C with the brace-balanced content of its last \\boxed{ (if the box never closes, everything after it). Layout = finished, wrong, C non-empty and rln4_lib.agree(C, gold). Finished rows with null n_new are dropped (none seen). M_F pools all finished rows including layout rows; even counts use the mean of the two middle values; statistic = M_L / M_F. Ambiguities: (1) Cleaning is literal, with no re-strip between steps, so 'C non-empty' can pass on leftover whitespace. alt_measured uses looser cleaning (strip after each step, all trailing '.' removed), which can change which rows are layout rows. (2) 'generated tokens' is taken as n_new (inventory: n_new = generated tokens); n_generated = n_new + 1 would barely move the ratio. n = number of layout rows, the smallest group. The bootstrap resamples (set, problem_index) units, each a tuple of up to 4 finished rows from the 4 files of that set. A resample with no layout rows scores 0.0, which pulls the lower interval bound down if layout rows are few (the recipe reports the number anyway when there are fewer than 5). The groups line also reports the layout-row count. refuted_by is null, so refuted_by_met is always false.
